claims.text: AsyncMongoClient must stay within a single event loop and cannot be shared across threads or event loops. (medium confidence)
The migration replaces the Motor client import with from pymongo import AsyncMongoClient; update client type annotations too. (medium confidence)
MongoDB describes PyMongo Async as native asyncio support, replacing Motor’s thread-pool network execution. (low confidence)
The migration guide warns that switching from Motor can degrade performance: native `asyncio` tasks do not guarantee a speedup for every workload. (low confidence)

Migration requires checking removed APIs: `AsyncMongoClient.__init__()` rejects `io_loop`; `AsyncCursor.each()` and `MotorGridOut.stream_to_handler()` are absent; replace `AsyncCursor.to_list(0)` with `to_list(None)`. (low confidence)
Mirage’s migration PR reports that aggregate(), list_indexes(), and watch() need awaiting before iteration under PyMongo Async; these methods returned cursors directly under Motor. (low confidence)

Agno’s migration follow-up explicitly fixes AsyncMongoDb.close() to await AsyncMongoClient.close(), and closes clients before simulated event-loop changes to prevent orphaned background tasks. This is evidence of a merged fix, not a claim about an installed release. (low confidence)
Mirage changed test fakes from MagicMock to AsyncMock, asserted awaits on cursor-producing methods, and added coverage of the change-stream path during migration. (low confidence)

Beanie’s 2.0.0 release switches from Motor to PyMongo Async and renames Document.get_motor_collection() to Document.get_pymongo_collection(); ODM callers therefore need to check wrapper API changes as well as driver imports. (low confidence)

Mongoz’s modernization guide requires removing Motor imports and dependencies and adopting native asynchronous types; its Registry binds to the event loop on first database use and must close asynchronously. (low confidence)

MongoDB’s Motor overview states deprecation began May 14, 2025, ordinary bug fixes ended May 14, 2026, and critical fixes end May 14, 2027. The cached PyMongo migration guide instead labels May 14th, 2026 as the deprecation date. These are conflicting page statements, not interchangeable lifecycle terms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB’s Motor overview and repository announce no new features, ordinary bug fixes until May 14, 2026, and critical fixes until final support ends May 14, 2027. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
